title: What Comes Back for a Stopped Catalogue Order, and When the Delivery Charge Goes With It
content:
Whether the delivery charge comes back along with the value of the items on a stopped catalogue order against a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card turns on how soon the member asks and on whether the order has gone out.

**How the day is read.** The day the order was placed is read from the order's own record, which carries that day and no time of day, so the deadline is settled in whole days and never in hours. The member asks on the day the order was placed where 0 whole days stand between the day the order was placed and the day they ask; they ask after that day where 1 or more whole days stand between the two.

**The rule.** What comes back is the value of the items together with the delivery charge the order carried, where the member asks for the order to be stopped on the day it was placed and it has not been despatched; it is the value of the items alone, where the member asks after that day and it has not been despatched, the plan having already paid for the despatch; and nothing comes back until the goods are returned in every other case.

| An order stands on the card, not yet despatched | Whole days since the day the order was placed | What comes back |
|---|---|---|
| yes | 0 | the value of the items together with the delivery charge the order carried |
| yes | 1 or more | the value of the items alone |
| no order stands | any | nothing comes back until the goods are returned |

**Worked through on hypothetical figures.** A standing order whose items came to 46.50 USD and which carried a delivery charge of 5.95 USD, stopped on the day it was placed: what comes back is 52.45 USD. The same order stopped a day later: what comes back is 46.50 USD, the plan having already paid for the despatch. Where no order stands against the card at all, nothing comes back until the goods are returned.
